full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 27.01.2009 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 380 of 1996 allowing the appeal in part arising out of judgment and decree dated 27.06.1996 passed in Title Suit No. 350 of 1990 by the Subordinate Judge, in-charge, Third Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka, decreeing the suit in part. 

 5. The trial Court by judgment and order dated 27.06.1996 decreed the suit in part. 

 6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with judgment and decree of the trial Court decreeing the suit in part, the plaintiff-bank filed First Appeal No. 380 of 1996 before the High Court Division. The High Court Division by its judgment and decree dated 27.01.2009 allowed the appeal in part with costs setting aside the impugned judgment and decree of the trial Court. 

 7. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with judgment and decree of the High Court Division, the leave petitioner filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal before this Division. 

 8. Mr. Sayyid Shahid Hussain, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the leave petitioner, submits that the High Court Division and the trial Court acted illegally in refusing to grant mortgage decree against respondent Nos.4 and 5 inasmuch as it appears from the record that respondent Nos. 2, 4 and 5 committed fraud upon the plaintiff-bank in obtaining huge loan placing the property in question as mortgage and that in consideration of this special fact, the High Court Division as well as the trial Court ought to have decreed the suit against respondent Nos. 4 and 5. He further submits that respondent Nos. 4 and 5 having not challenged the mortgage of the property after being major for a long time, in fact, accepted the action of their father mortgaging the property to the plaintiff-bank and that both the Courts acted illegally in not considering this aspect of the case and in not distinguishing the facts of the case Sri Kakulam Surahmanyam and another Vs. Kurra Subba Rao, AIR 1948 (PC) 95.
